clue.text: Jump across, initially moving right to left, to arrive at different levels

indicators.note: moving says one letter of the built word changes its position
to left says the shifted letter travels leftwards, towards the front of the word

parts.note: to jump in surprise is to start

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word across

explanation.surface: A gymnastics or parkour instruction: leap across, shifting right to left, to land on different platforms.
explanation.walkthrough: START plus A (across, initially) gives STARTA; 'moving right to left' shifts its R one place leftwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, the stacked bands of rock or society lying at different heights.

clue.text: Beginning to beat out precious metal, striking head

parts.note: to thresh is to beat grain out of its husks

indicators.note: striking the head off a word removes its first letter

parts.note: gold is a precious metal

explanation.surface: A goldsmith starts hammering out precious metal, hitting it on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' looks like an instruction but is the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the doorway step, and figuratively the point of starting something.

clue.text: Sharp police unit infiltrating revolutionary spies

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one piece enters the other
revolutionary suggests turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency
the CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A sharp police squad gets in among a group of rebel spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses the agency's initials to AIC; 'infiltrating' puts the British detectives inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic tastes or flavours are sour and sharp; it also means cutting in tone.

clue.text: A rector overseeing organ recital, originally raised church's sense of superiority

indicators.note: overseeing in a down clue means sitting above, so these pieces come first
raised in a down clue says that letter is lifted higher in the word

parts.note: the word organ taken as written

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of recital

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A vicar presides over an organ recital that starts the church congregation feeling superior.
explanation.walkthrough: In ORGAN the letter R (recital, originally) is 'raised' one place, giving ROGAN, below A and R, above CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is an overbearing pride, a feeling of being better than others.

clue.text: Finishing touches for scripts by Dan Levy, showing correct use of language

indicators.note: the finishing touches of words are their final letters, taken here from three words

parts.note: a levy is a tax

explanation.surface: Dan Levy, the Schitt's Creek writer, polishing his scripts so the grammar is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Levy' looks like part of the writer's name; it is the synonym for TAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the set of rules for arranging words correctly into sentences.

clue.text: Rearing mountain lions making a university review …

indicators.note: rearing means rising up, so in a down clue the letters are read upwards
making a into university swaps that letter for the abbreviation

parts.note: pumas are also known as mountain lions

explanation.surface: Big cats rearing up on a campus, leading into a review of the next clue's scene.
explanation.walkthrough: PUMAS with its A made U is PUMUS, which 'Rearing' reads upwards. The ellipsis links into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum up is to summarise or recap, just as a review goes over the main points.

clue.text: … new animal sanctuary — first to accept incarceration, essentially will make most irritable

parts.note: Noah's ark was a refuge for the animals

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: first is written 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the very centre letter of incarceration

explanation.surface: Continuing the zoo story: a new animal refuge where locking creatures up makes them grumpiest.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST, read as IST, takes in E, the central letter of INCARCERATION. NARKY is British slang for irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Narky is informal British for bad-tempered, so the superlative means the crossest.

clue.text: Brussels supports aid arrangement for so long

indicators.note: supports in a down clue means sitting underneath
an arrangement puts the letters into a fresh order

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, standing for it

explanation.surface: The European Union backs an aid deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels for EU is metonymy, the capital standing for the institution based there.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, as is the casual farewell so long.

clue.text: TV show judge's entertaining pooch?

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a judge is one who tries cases, a trier
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: A television talent judge has a dog on as a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: a terrier is just one kind of pooch.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of dog, and pooch is a casual word for any dog.

clue.text: Perhaps Harrovians and partners, entering drag race

indicators.note: entering means going into, so this piece sits within the others

parts.note: to drag a vehicle is to tow it
a race is a people or nation
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Harrow schoolboys and their partners take part in a drag race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrovians' suggests pupils of Harrow School, but here they are the residents of Harrow, a town in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of a town are its townspeople, and Harrovians live in Harrow.

clue.text: Can I spoil first drink

indicators.note: first puts this piece at the front, ahead of the other two

parts.note: to spoil something is to mar it
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether they may ruin things by having a drink first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can I' reads as a request, but 'Can' is TIN and 'I' stays itself; 'first' moves MAR to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Most of river reaches English channel eventually

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan
a channel cut for water is a course

explanation.surface: A river that, nearly in full, finally flows into the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English channel' reads as the sea strait between England and France; the words split into E and COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: In due course means at the appropriate time, later on, which is eventually.

clue.text: Clue to make WAG punish cleaner

parts.note: read the answer as a clue: WASHING-UP rearranged ('liquid' as the signal that letters flow into a new order) gives WAG PUNISH

explanation.surface: A note on how to write a clue that turns a footballer's wife into a disciplinarian.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer itself works as a clue whose result is WAG PUNISH, with LIQUID as the anagram signal on WASHING UP. A WAG is a footballer's wife or girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing-up liquid is the detergent used to clean dishes after a meal.

clue.text: See Mark's predicament

definitions.meaning: to be in a tight situation

explanation.surface: An invitation to look at the trouble someone called Mark is in.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: notice, a stain, and a tricky situation as in a tight spot.

clue.text: Stable's opening tack room — it's slow

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a tack is a small nail
room in the sense of space to move

explanation.surface: At a stables, the first stop is the tack room, where saddles hang, and it is a sluggish place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack room' reads as one stables term, but the two words work separately. 'opening' takes the first letter of Stable's.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail's pace is a proverbially slow speed, so the phrase describes something slow.

clue.text: After baffling air raid film, turned shed light on

indicators.note: baffling means confusing, so these letters are thrown into disorder
turned means flipped round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: Someone switched off a confusing war film about an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baffling' rearranges AIR RAID to IRRADIA; 'turned' reverses ET to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To irradiate is to expose to radiation or illuminate, to cast rays on something.

clue.text: Stunned banks withdraw from Mae West fight

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outer letters, and they leave

parts.note: a ruck is a brawl or scuffle

explanation.surface: Startled financial institutions pull out of a boxing match involving Mae West.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West was a Hollywood star; with her first name's outer letters gone, A is left. RUCK is British slang for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means filled with wonder, stopped in one's tracks, like someone stunned.

clue.text: Sick have small portion under doctor — it might well be boring

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts these pieces below the other

parts.note: sick means ill
a bit is a small portion

explanation.surface: An ill patient gets a small dose from the doctor, which may prove tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like 'quite possibly' but is the noun: a drill bit bores wells.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill bit is the cutting tip used to bore holes, such as a well shaft.

clue.text: After five Americans leave bar area ready, ale's drunk — and some kind of wine?

indicators.note: drunk means mixed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to leave is to depart, so those letters are taken out of the fodder

parts.note: ale's is read as ale is; the word ale goes into the mix
A is an abbreviation for American, so five Americans are five A's

explanation.surface: Five American drinkers walk out of a bar once the ale is gone, leaving the question of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the five A's from BAR AREA READY ALE, leaving BRREREDYLE; 'drunk' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderberries are fermented to make country wine, so the fruit names a kind of homemade wine.

clue.text: Note start of month has new moon, occasionally

indicators.note: start of asks for the opening letter of month
occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A diary note that the month begins with a new moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of NEW MOON: E, M, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note or reminder.

clue.text: Small change for policeman

definitions.meaning: ... are low-value coins, British pennies made of ...

explanation.surface: A small alteration made for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a low-value brown coin, and a slang term for an officer.

clue.text: Broadcast porn deal matters for pair that grind

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that an adult film deal is being aired on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle and mortar are the two tools used together to crush spices.

clue.text: Kitsch outfit dismissed with a sound

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothes, an outfit

explanation.surface: A tacky outfit is rejected with a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A schwa is the unstressed neutral vowel sound, as at the start of about.

clue.text: Nervous, puzzling 5 across, 10 down

indicators.note: puzzling means bewildering, so the remaining letters are jumbled
down here means taken down, removed from the word

parts.note: the answer to 5 across is used as the fodder
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone anxious, baffled by the grid references 5 across and 10 down.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 down' looks like the cross-reference, but means X removed from SYNTAX; 'puzzling' rearranges SYNTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Antsy is informal for restless and fidgety, as if having ants in one's pants.

clue.text: Discovered this book with way-out jacket for present

indicators.note: a jacket wraps around, so one piece goes outside the others

parts.note: the way out of a building is the exit

indicators.note: discovered means with the cover off, so the outer letters of this are removed

explanation.surface: A find of an eccentric dust jacket on a book, offered as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' strips the cover letters off this; 'jacket' wraps the way out around. 'Present' is the verb, to show.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit is to show or display publicly, which is one sense of to present.

clue.text: Small bottle found in a drug smuggler containing cannabis, mostly

indicators.note: containing means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a mule is someone who carries drugs across a border

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Customs find a small bottle on a courier who was carrying most of a cannabis haul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the slang word; 'containing' puts what remains inside the smuggler.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule is a small sealed glass vial, typically holding a dose of medicine.

clue.text: Books Lineker, say, without support

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Gary Lineker, the footballer and broadcaster, is one example of a Gary
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Gary Lineker's books selling with no backing behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside. Gary Lineker is an English football star turned TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a frame or bridge structure that supports cranes, signals or rocket equipment.

clue.text: Article on excited UK Green insiders' legendary response to rising water level

definitions.text: legendary response to rising water level

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after what it follows
excited means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged
insiders are the letters inside a word, without its ends

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Green Party insider in Britain thrilled at a news item on rising water levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insiders'' takes the middle of Green and 'excited' stirs it with the country's letters; 'on' places the article after.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes supposedly shouted eureka when his bath water rose and he grasped displacement.
